summary: FlameAtlas is an interactive, SI-powered dashboard that turns decades of NASA microgravity combustion research into fire safety guidance for the Moon, Mars and orbit. We used Claude, a Super Intelligence tool, to brainstorm and code the site and extract data from 30 NASA and peer-reviewed sources; our team checked every number against its source. The site summarizes 24 key findings, ranks them for any mission scenario, and interprets them through a Flame Lab, a Mission Risk Console with cited actions and safer material swaps, an evidence-gap map, and a live SI assistant that answers only from the findings, with citations. We also analysed 129 raw ISS tests from NASA's BASS-II record ourselves and found that thick acrylic released about 17 times more carbon monoxide than fabric. This matters because Earth tests can mislead: acrylic that goes out at 16% oxygen on Earth kept burning at 13.6% on the ISS, and future habitats plan a 34% oxygen atmosphere. FlameAtlas shows designers what is risky, what to do, and which 55 of 72 cases no one has tested yet. It is free and open source.
details: FlameAtlas is an interactive dashboard that turns NASA's microgravity combustion research into fire safety guidance for the Moon, Mars and orbit. We collected 30 NASA and peer-reviewed sources, including NASA Physical Sciences Informatics records (BASS, BASS-II, FLEX, ACME, Saffire, SAME, DAFT) and NTRS papers. Claude, a Super Intelligence tool, helped us brainstorm and code the site and extract data, and our team checked every number against its source. The site summarizes 24 key findings and ranks them for any mission by relevance, strength of evidence and safety impact. It interprets them through a Flame Lab showing how flames behave in different gravity, a Mission Risk Console that scores a scenario and suggests cited actions and safer materials, an evidence-gap map, and a live SI assistant that answers only from the findings, with citations. We also analysed 129 raw ISS tests ourselves and found that thick acrylic released about 17 times more carbon monoxide than fabric. The intended impact is to help habitat designers choose materials, safety teams plan fire response, and agencies decide what to test next: 55 of 72 material, oxygen and gravity combinations have no data, and no Mars-gravity case has been tested. We built it with HTML, CSS and plain JavaScript, hosted it free on GitHub Pages, and run the assistant on Cloudflare Workers AI with the open-source Llama 3.1 8B model. We prioritized accuracy and honesty: every number is traceable, uncertain results are marked low confidence, and our risk index agrees with flight results. It costs nothing to run, works on phones and keyboards, and still answers when networks such as METU Wi-Fi block the assistant.
